pair_convention.spot_explanation: USD/CHF at 0.80763 means 1 USD = 0.80763 CHF. Rising = USD strengthening vs CHF. Falling = CHF appreciating vs USD. Note that the quote dossier is written from the franc's perspective, where 'Bearish CHF' is the same statement as 'Bullish USD/CHF'. All such statements have been translated into pair direction in this report.
pair_convention.bearish_means: pair FALLS (USD weakens vs CHF; the franc appreciates)
pair_convention.base_dossier_tactical_stance: USD — dossier stance: tactical Bullish, conviction 3, net score +0.3440 (ranked 1st of 11 in the G10+SGD set); strategic Neutral with a bullish tilt, conviction 2, +0.1032
pair_convention.quote_dossier_tactical_stance: CHF — dossier stance: tactical Bearish, conviction 3, net score −0.2358 (ranked 9th of 11); strategic Neutral, conviction 2, −0.0499. Translated to pair direction, the franc dossier is tactically bullish USD/CHF and strategically neutral.

executive_summary: USD/CHF trades at 0.80763 as of the 2026-09-03 payload close, which is two trading days after the 2026-09-01 valuation date and is the anchor for every level, target and pip calculation in this report. The pair has gone almost nowhere over one month (+0.07%) while grinding higher over longer windows — +1.22% over three months, +3.58% over six and +2.83% over one year — and it sits at the 78th percentile of its 52-week closing range (0.76602–0.81938), a firm but not extended reading. The dominant bilateral narrative is the widest positive carry the dollar holds anywhere in the G10: a 362.5bp policy differential against a franc pinned at 0.00% by an SNB conditional forecast conditioned on that rate through 2028, with a scheduled opportunity to widen to 387.5bp on 16 September. What diverges most sharply from the standalone dossiers is that Switzerland's own fundamentals are the best in years — Q2 GDP at +1.5% quarter-on-quarter, a KOF barometer at a four-and-a-half-year high, a July trade surplus of CHF 8.1bn that is the largest since the series began in 1950, and July real retail sales at +2.3% year-on-year against an expected 1.3% — and none of it buys a rate rise, so its transmission to spot is weak while US core PCE at 3.3% transmits directly through the front end. Bilaterally the pair has also acquired a new structural driver that neither dossier captures: with low volatility sustaining carry trades, the franc is increasingly preferred over the yen as a funding currency, a CHF-funded Mexican peso carry returning roughly 4% over the past month against about 1.3% for the same trade funded in yen. The settled verdict is tactically Bullish, conviction 3, net weighted score +0.3964, and strategically Bullish, conviction 2, +0.1132 — a score clearing the Neutral boundary by only 1.3 points. The caveat is the pair's own option skew, which contradicts the direction at every tenor: 25-delta risk reversals of −0.528%, −0.506% and −0.602% mean the market pays continuously for USD/CHF downside, and with 20-day realised volatility at 8.67% against one-month implied of 6.852%, the tail is both cheap and already moving.

market_context.valuation_assessment: Pair-level valuation is genuinely contested and both available measures are proxies rather than models. The base dossier's BIS-REER-relative table implies a USD/CHF fair value of 0.7623 — the dollar 6.05% expensive against the franc in real terms; the quote dossier's REER-momentum proxy implies 0.8028, the dollar roughly 0.82% cheap and essentially fair. The two disagree by 5.3% and neither is a purchasing-power-parity calculation, so the honest reading is that the pair is somewhere between fair and modestly rich for the dollar, with no valuation urgency in either direction. The underlying real-exchange-rate inputs are a US BIS REER of 107.84 for June 2026 against a Swiss reading of 101.69, the dollar sitting at an estimated 78th percentile of its post-2015 range and the franc at the 40th percentile of a 30-month window — both percentiles internal estimates rather than published statistics. Set against the pair's own multi-year history the picture inverts entirely: USD/CHF traded above 1.0011 in October 2022, its heaviest computed supply band at 0.91480–0.92045 carries six touches and sits 1,100 pips (13.62%) above spot, and the pair has not closed above its 200-week average in 84 consecutive weeks. What is priced at 0.80763 is a world in which the 362.5bp differential persists and no haven bid materialises — both true today, both already in the price at the 78th range percentile.

market_context.recent_regime: The regime since June has been a carry grind interrupted once, violently. The pair rose almost continuously from a 0.78103 close on 29 May to a 0.81938 close on 28 July and an intraday 52-week high of 0.82072 on 29 July, then lost 0.80401 on 30 July and has since traded a 0.79697–0.81571 band — a two-month consolidation at the top of a six-month advance, with a higher low (0.79697 on 19 August, well above May's 0.77955) but no new high. The interruption is the 19 August session, and its cause is bilateral rather than macro: Chris Turner at ING explains that USD/CHF's sharp drop after the US Treasury buy-back announcement was mainly position adjustment after a hawkish Fed narrative had favoured longs, recalling April 2025 when concerns over US policy credibility hit all US asset classes and both the dollar and the franc were preferred. Since then the pair has recovered steadily — 0.80944 on the Warsh day, 0.81163 on 1 September, 0.81298 on 2 September after tagging 0.81571 — before a 79-pip reversal on 3 September closed at 0.80763 in the lower half of the day's range, a rejection at the two-touch supply band that leaves the consolidation intact.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The annualised carry on a long USD/CHF position is +362.5bp, the widest positive carry the dollar holds against any currency in the G10+SGD set: a 3.50–3.75% federal funds target range with a 3.625% midpoint against an SNB policy rate of 0.00%. On the June-vintage monthly series the ten-year differential is +416bp, the widest long-end gap either dossier identifies anywhere. At the 0.80763 payload spot, 3.625% is worth 292.8 pips a year, 24.1 pips over 30 days, 73.2 pips over three months and 146.4 pips over six. The carry-to-vol ratio is 0.516 (3.625/7.031% 3M ATM implied vol); against 60-day realised of 7.27% the ratio is 0.499 and against 20-day realised of 8.67% it is 0.418 — the best risk-adjusted carry available in the dollar complex, with deterioration as the volatility window shortens embedded as a warning. The carry regime is working: VIX at 14.43–14.51, tight credit spreads, and a near-zero EUR/USD cross-currency basis describe exactly the low-volatility, no-funding-stress condition in which borrowing a zero-rate currency accrues. The franc is the funding leg by construction and its role as a funding currency is growing as participants rotate away from a yen exposed to intervention risk. The regime breaks not when carry stops paying but when realised volatility rises enough to make it uneconomic, and 20-day realised at 8.67% against 6.852% implied says that process may already have begun. Forward points derive from a −415.8bp annualised futures-implied roll premium, roughly 53.3bp wider than the policy differential — a residual of basis plus money-market spread that cannot be separated without an OIS curve — meaning a rolled long must clear roughly 4.16% annualised rather than 3.62% simply to break even.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: High-carry pair: the 362.5bp policy differential is the widest positive carry the dollar holds against any currency in the G10+SGD set and the widest carry deficit the franc runs against any peer bar AUD and NOK. On a pair where one leg is pinned at zero by an explicit multi-year commitment, the rate differential is not one input among ten — it is the transmission mechanism through which most of the others express themselves. Boosted +0.03 on both horizons, inside the framework's ±0.05 limit.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral differential is 362.5bp in the dollar's favour — a 3.50-3.75% federal funds target range against an SNB policy rate of 0.00% — and on the June monthly vintage of both legs the ten-year differential is 416bp, the widest long-end gap either dossier identifies anywhere in its peer set. The direction of travel over the next four weeks is either flat or wider, never narrower, and that asymmetry is scheduled rather than speculative: the FOMC meets on 16 September with a Summary of Economic Projections attached and futures price roughly 57-66% odds of a 25bp increase to 3.75-4.00%, which would take the differential to 387.5bp, while the SNB meets eight days later on 24 September having conditioned its entire three-year conditional inflation forecast (0.6% for 2026, 0.6% for 2027, 0.7% for 2028) on the policy rate remaining at zero throughout. There is no plausible mechanism by which the quote leg moves toward the base leg inside the tactical window. The transmission to spot is the cleanest in the G10: with the franc the only zero-rate currency in the set and 100bp below the next-lowest, USD/CHF is the highest-yielding major expression of a long-dollar position, and the confirming independent evidence is the 2-year Treasury at 4.34%, which sits 71.5bp above the 3.625% policy midpoint and cannot be reconciled with a hold-then-cut path. The one genuine offset is that the carry is fully known and has been for a year, so the marginal information is the change rather than the level — and the change is what 16 September delivers.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the differential stops widening but does not close, and the asymmetry of the two legs is what keeps the stance Bullish at reduced confidence. On the base leg the Committee's own June projections carry a 2026 median of 3.8% and a 2027 median of 3.6%, which makes a September increase terminal rather than the start of a cycle — so the dollar's rate advantage plateaus near 387.5bp through the 28 October and 9 December decisions and begins to decay only in 2027. On the quote leg nothing can move at all: Swiss headline CPI is 0.4% and core 0.3%, the conditional forecast is conditioned on zero through 2028, Chairman Schlegel has repeatedly cited the undesirable side effects of negative rates, and the SNB meets only twice more inside the window, on 24 September and 10 December, at each of which a hold is the overwhelming base case. The bilateral consequence is that the pair's carry becomes a static rather than a deteriorating input — it stops generating new dollar strength and simply becomes a 3.6-3.9% annual hurdle that any franc-bullish thesis must clear. That is a materially weaker impulse than the tactical one, which is why confidence falls fourteen points, but it is still positive: at 362.5bp against a zero-rate leg with a 7.031% three-month implied volatility, the carry-to-vol ratio of 0.516 is the best risk-adjusted carry available in the dollar complex.

factors.horizon_split: Both horizons are Bullish for the pair and the stance is identical, but confidence falls from 74 to 60 for a mechanical reason: inside four weeks the differential has a scheduled opportunity to widen by 25bp on 16 September with nothing on the calendar capable of narrowing it, whereas over one to six months the Fed's own 2027 median of 3.6% turns the same differential into a level that persists and then decays. The tactical horizon captures the repricing into the hike; the strategic horizon captures the plateau after it.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential is the largest of any pair either dossier covers and it runs entirely one way: US headline CPI 3.4% and core PCE 3.3% — unmoved for three consecutive months — with headline PCE at 3.7% and a six-month annualised rate of 4.1%, against Swiss headline CPI of 0.4% and core of 0.3%. That is roughly 300bp of core inflation differential, and its importance for this pair is not the level but the asymmetry of the reaction functions attached to it: 3.3% core PCE forces the Fed toward a hike, while 0.3% Swiss core buys the SNB nothing at all. The growth differential cuts the other way and must be stated honestly, because it is the single strongest argument against the pair rising: Swiss Q2 GDP grew 1.5% quarter-on-quarter against a 0.2-0.4% consensus, the KOF barometer printed 106.7 in August (its highest since November 2021), industrial production ran +5.5% year-on-year against a -4.7% forecast, and Swiss GDP of 2.33% year-on-year on the OECD vintage exceeds the US 2.10%. Switzerland is currently the better economy and the better surprise generator. But growth that produces no inflation cannot produce a policy response, so the transmission of Swiss strength to spot is limited to equity and direct-investment flows, whereas US inflation transmits directly through the front end. The asymmetric sensitivity is therefore that US data — 4 September payrolls at +58,000 consensus after -23,000, and 11 September CPI — moves this pair several times harder than the 3 September Swiss GDP and CPI double-header, and the tactical skew is dollar-positive with a fat left tail on payrolls.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months both sides of the differential decay and the honest bilateral verdict is Neutral. On the base leg the inflation that is forcing the Fed's hand is substantially tariff-driven at an average statutory rate of 11.0%, which is a one-off price level effect that drops out of the year-on-year comparison, while the labour deterioration — payrolls at -23,000, wage growth at a five-year low, participation falling, ISM non-manufacturing employment at 47.4 — is a trend rather than an artefact. On the quote leg Switzerland's apparent strength is very likely borrowed: US Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs of up to 15% were announced on 2 April and took effect on 31 July, chemical and pharmaceutical exports jumped 25.7% in July, and exports pulled forward ahead of a tariff are exports that will not happen in Q4 and Q1 — which is why the IMF carries 0.8% for 2026 and the SNB 'around 1%' against a 1.5% quarterly run-rate. So the pair faces a base leg whose inflation premium fades and a quote leg whose growth premium fades, roughly simultaneously and to roughly offsetting effect. The one durable asymmetry is that Swiss inflation of 0.4% mechanically produces real franc appreciation over time even with a soft nominal rate, which is the structural counterweight this factor cannot resolve at a 0.10 weight and which is properly captured in Factor 5 instead.

factors.horizon_split: The stance moves from Bullish to Neutral because the two legs' current data strengths have the same expiry date and opposite signs. Tactically the Fed reacts to a core PCE print of 3.3% that has not moved in three months while the SNB cannot react to Swiss growth of any magnitude, so the inflation differential dominates. Strategically the tariff component doing the work in US core PCE is a level effect with a defined life, and the pharmaceutical front-running doing the work in Swiss GDP reverses inside the same window — so the same dataset that is emphatically pair-positive over four weeks is genuinely two-sided over six months.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Haven-versus-haven pair: both legs are bid in a risk-off episode, which mutes the pair's net risk beta relative to a haven-versus-risk-proxy cross like AUD/JPY. USD/CHF belongs in the low-to-moderate risk-sensitivity bucket and the offsetting betas mean the factor carries less bilateral information than the default weight implies. Reduced −0.03 tactically and −0.02 strategically to fund the Factor 1 increase.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is a haven-versus-haven pair, so the standard risk-beta framing has to be replaced with a question about which haven wins at the margin — and in the current regime neither is being bid, which is not symmetric in its effect. The franc's only role in a benign tape is as the zero-rate funding leg, so calm actively works against it; the dollar loses its haven premium in calm but retains a 3.625% policy rate and live US exceptionalism, so calm costs it far less. With VIX at 14.43-14.51 after falling between 3.7 and 6.2 points on the month, investment-grade spreads at 79bp, high yield at 260-263bp and 27bp tighter, and equities near cycle highs, the funding-currency channel dominates the haven channel and the net effect is pair-positive. The confirming cross-sectional evidence is in the franc's own crosses — AUD/CHF at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range, CHF/NOK at the 2nd — which is the same rotation seen from a different angle. The dissenting signal is important and deserves stating: gold at 4,456.44 is up 8.6-9.9% on the month and 22.4% on the year, and the franc's traditional correlate being bought hard while the franc is sold is a correlation breakdown, most plausibly because a currency paying 0% with an explicit official cap on it is a poor vehicle for a debasement hedge. That reads as franc haven demand being under-bid rather than absent, which is why confidence is 55 rather than higher.

What is not priced is that from these levels the VIX distribution is skewed almost entirely higher, and a haven-versus-haven pair resolves that skew ambiguously rather than in the dollar's favour.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the compression that makes this factor tactically pair-positive becomes the reason it cannot be extrapolated, and the haven-versus-haven structure makes the sign of any reversal genuinely indeterminate. At 79bp investment grade and 260-263bp high yield there is far more room for spreads to widen than to tighten, and the mean-reverting path is a risk-off episode — but in a risk-off episode both legs are bid, and which one wins depends on the character of the shock rather than its size. A pure equity or geopolitical shock historically favours the franc, which would push the pair lower; a dollar funding or liquidity shock favours the dollar decisively, which would push it sharply higher and is the specific configuration Factor 10 identifies as building into year-end. The two candidate shocks point in opposite directions for this pair, and both dossiers identify credible triggers for each — an unresolved Middle East conflict on one side, reserve balances at $2,916bn with no reverse-repo buffer on the other. Add the SNB's explicit willingness to intervene against rapid franc appreciation, which truncates the right tail of any franc haven rally, and the honest strategic verdict is Neutral: the factor will not drive the pair higher from an already-compressed starting point, and it cannot be relied on to drive it lower either.

Strategically the reversal is more likely than the continuation, and because both legs are havens the pair's response to that reversal depends on the character of the shock rather than its arrival, which is not something we can call.

Dollar Index non-commercial net length is 18,682 contracts as of 25 August, down 3,817 or roughly 17% across four consecutive weeks from a 22,499 peak on 4 August described as a three-and-a-half-year high, and every tranche of that reduction predates Warsh's 28 August keynote. Neutral is the honest net.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the two legs stop cancelling and start reinforcing each other in the same direction - downward for the pair - which is why the stance turns Bearish. On the base leg the relevant flow ceases to be weekly futures and becomes reserve-manager allocation: the dollar's share of allocated reserves is 57.13%, some fifteen percentage points below its 2001 peak, and speculative length enters the window from a three-and-a-half-year high, so the distribution of positioning change is skewed toward reduction simply because there is more room to sell than to buy. On the quote leg the concentrated asset-manager short of -38,322 contracts against total open interest of only 109,874 is the classic funding-currency configuration - real money is the persistent structural seller and dealers are the long counterparty - and real-money shorts of that size are slow to build and slower to unwind, which makes them squeeze fuel rather than a stop-loss. The bilateral arithmetic is stark: roughly 10,000 contracts of room to extend the franc short before the notable threshold binds, against combined speculative exposure near 49,800 contracts that would have to be bought back in a squeeze. That is the raw material of every violent franc appreciation in the record, and the January 2015 floor removal is the reference for magnitude. Confidence is only 52 because the trigger is exogenous and undated, and because the SNB's stated willingness to intervene against rapid appreciation, backed by CHF 889.6bn of official reserve assets, caps the squeeze even if it cannot prevent it.

tactical.contrarian_case: The case against a long USD/CHF here is that it is a consensus trade being added to at an unfavourable point on both legs: the dollar is being bought for a hike that prediction markets price at only 48-55%, and the franc is being sold at the weak end of its ranges against most of the G10 after a 3.3% six-month depreciation against the dollar. Meanwhile the pair's own option market pays a persistent premium for downside at every tenor, which is a well-informed constituency taking the other side.

strategic.historical_analogue: January 2015, when the removal of the EUR/CHF floor moved that pair roughly 30% intraday from a comparably one-sided structural short. The magnitude is not the base case — the SNB now has CHF 889.6bn of reserves and a stated willingness to lean against appreciation, which did not exist in the same form then — but the mechanism is identical.
strategic.contrarian_case: The strategic contrarian position is to own the pair's downside rather than its direction. A currency running a 9.77%-of-GDP current account, a AAA sovereign at 37.6% debt-to-GDP and a concentrated real-money short against it does not stay cheap indefinitely, and at 7.187% six-month implied volatility the option market is charging for a one-standard-deviation move of roughly 5% in a pair whose defining historical feature is the jump. The consensus long is being paid 362.5bp a year to be short that jump.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external differential on this pair is the widest in either dossier's peer set and it runs entirely against the pair: Switzerland is running a current account of 9.77% of GDP against a US deficit of 2.85%, a gap of some 12.6 percentage points, and the bilateral relationship is a direct franc bid - IMF Direction of Trade Statistics show the US importing $63.7bn of goods from Switzerland in 2024 against $25.0bn of exports, a $38.6bn US goods deficit with a country of nine million people. The tactical relevance, despite the low 0.06 weight, is that both legs produced fresh extremes this month in opposite directions: Switzerland posted a July trade surplus of CHF 8.1bn, the largest since the series began in January 1950, on exports up 13.8% and imports down 4.5%, while the US advance goods balance came in at -$118.8bn against a -$100.8bn forecast, an $18bn single-month deterioration. The transmission over four weeks is weak - a monthly trade print does not move a G10 pair - but the direction is unambiguous, and the 17 September Swiss trade release is a dated tactical test of whether the surplus is structural or tariff front-running. On terms of trade the pair is near-symmetric and mildly pair-positive: the US is a net energy exporter and Switzerland a net energy importer, so Brent's fall from 100.31 to 88.24 is a modest terms-of-trade gain for the quote leg, which is the one commodity channel working against the pair this month.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.16 strategic weight this is the largest single negative on the pair and the arithmetic compounds rather than mean-reverts. Switzerland's 9.77%-of-GDP current account is structural - a goods surplus in pharmaceuticals, precision engineering and watches, a services surplus in financial and commodity-trading revenue, and a primary income surplus thrown off by a net international investment position of CHF 974bn worth roughly 120% of annual GDP - and it generates a continuous, price-insensitive excess of franc receipts over franc payments that must be repatriated, hedged, or absorbed by the SNB. The mirror image on the base leg is deteriorating in exactly the way that matters: the US deficit widened to 2.9% of GDP in Q1 with the primary income balance flipping from surplus to deficit, which attacks the specific exorbitant-privilege mechanism that has allowed a -$21.27trn investment position to coexist with a stable currency. Two genuine bilateral offsets keep confidence at 70 rather than higher, and both are pair-specific rather than generic. First, US Section 232 tariffs of up to 15% on Swiss pharmaceutical imports, effective 31 July, hit close to half of Swiss goods exports to the United States, and July's 25.7% surge in chemical and pharmaceutical exports is very likely front-running that reverses inside the window. Second, Switzerland has committed to facilitate at least USD 200bn of investment into the United States over five years, USD 67bn of it in 2026 - a directly bilateral outbound capital flow, franc-sold and dollar-bought, equal to a meaningful fraction of the annual surplus and the most underdiscussed pair-positive item in either dossier. Even netting both, a 12.6-point current-account differential does not reverse over six months.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: The US is now a net energy exporter, so oil higher is a mild positive for the dollar through terms of trade, though a larger negative through the inflation path — which in the current reaction function cuts in the dollar's favour anyway by reinforcing the hawkish case. Henry Hub at $2.70 is unremarkable. The dollar has no meaningful metals or agricultural exposure and its commodity beta is low.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: Switzerland is a net energy importer with no domestic production, so oil higher is a direct negative for the franc through terms of trade. Its dominant commodity linkage is gold: Switzerland is the world's largest refining hub, and gold at 4,456.44, up 8.6% on the month and 22.4% on the year, is the franc's principal correlate. Natural gas and LNG exposure runs through the European import channel and is franc-negative when prices rise.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Applying the framework's direction rules leg by leg: Oil up 10% — the base leg gets a mild positive as a net energy exporter (+) plus an indirect positive through an inflation impulse that reinforces the Fed's hawkish reaction function; the quote leg gets a clear negative as an importer with no offset (−). Base positive plus quote negative equals pair UP: oil higher is bullish USD/CHF, though modestly, since neither leg is a commodity currency and the transmission is second-order. Gold up 10% — the base leg is ambiguous, and the current episode shows gold and the dollar rising together, which the base dossier reads as a debasement hedge rather than a dollar-alternative trade; the quote leg gets a clear positive through both the refining-hub channel and the shared haven correlation (+CHF). Base neutral plus quote positive equals pair DOWN: gold higher is bearish USD/CHF, and gold is the larger and more reliable of the two channels for this pair. Natural gas up — quote leg negative via European import prices, base leg mildly positive as an LNG exporter, so pair UP. Netting all three at current trends — Brent down $12.07 on the month to 88.24 and gold up 8.6% — the live commodity impulse is bearish for the pair on both legs simultaneously, which is unusual and is one reason the external-balance factor is negative on both horizons.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent from 88.24 to roughly 97 — mildly bullish USD/CHF. The base leg gains modestly on terms of trade and more meaningfully through the inflation channel, since higher energy reinforces the case for the 16 September hike; the quote leg loses on import costs with no offset. Estimated net effect small, well under 1% on the pair, because neither leg is commodity-driven.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent from 88.24 to roughly 79 — mildly bearish USD/CHF. Switzerland's terms of trade improve as an importer while the US loses a modest export gain, and critically the disinflationary impulse undercuts the tactical case for the hike that is doing most of the work in Factor 1, so the second-order effect through the base leg's policy path is larger than the first-order terms-of-trade effect.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Gold, not oil. Gold is the franc's genuine correlate through the refining hub and the shared haven bid, and its 22.4% twelve-month rise while the dollar firmed is the single most informative commodity observation for this pair — it says the haven and debasement bid is being expressed in metal rather than in francs, which is currently pair-positive but describes under-bid franc demand rather than absent franc demand.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the rare pair where both central banks' communication points the same way, and the sequencing amplifies it. On the base leg the Fed is currently more hawkish than the curve: the June Summary of Economic Projections raised the 2026 median to 3.8% from 3.4%, implying a hike outright while futures price only 57-66%, nine participants backed continued hikes, and the July meeting produced a 9-3 hold in which all three dissenters wanted a 25bp increase - the first three-dissent meeting with a unified direction since September 2016. Warsh then used the 28 August Jackson Hole keynote to recommit to the 2% PCE objective as a firm, fixed target and to say the summer's better prints do not tell him underlying trends have meaningfully improved. On the quote leg the SNB has given the market something more useful than a rate path: an explicitly one-sided reaction function to the exchange rate, stating on 18 June and reaffirming on 8 July an increased willingness to intervene to counter rapid and excessive franc appreciation, with no corresponding commitment against depreciation and no plausible level of franc weakness at which a bank forecasting 0.6% inflation would object. For this pair that is a written option: the Fed says it will tighten if inflation persists and the SNB says it will sell francs if they rally. The sequence matters because the FOMC on 16 September precedes the SNB on 24 September by eight days, so the Fed sets the level and the SNB responds to it rather than the reverse. The two-sided tactical risk is specific and dated: after a 3.3% six-month franc depreciation against the dollar, the pressure the intervention sentence was written to counter has abated, and dropping or softening it on 24 September would be read as tolerance of a stronger franc.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months guidance nearly doubles in weight to 0.12 and remains the second-largest positive on the pair, because it is a statement about reaction functions rather than about data. On the quote leg the SNB's structural incentive to prefer a softer franc is reinforced rather than weakened inside the window: Swiss exports face a US pharmaceutical tariff of up to 15%, which raises rather than lowers the bank's sensitivity to any further loss of competitiveness through the exchange rate, and its stated tool preference is intervention rather than negative rates, backed by CHF 889.6bn of official reserve assets and the strongest FX-intervention record in the developed world. There are only two more assessments in the window, on 24 September and 10 December, and neither plausibly moves the rate. On the base leg the Fed has moved to meeting-by-meeting data dependence with decisions on 28 October and 9 December, the latter carrying a fresh SEP, and there is a reflexive dynamic the market does not price: political pressure to cut raises rather than lowers the institutional incentive to tighten when inflation justifies it, because the cost of appearing to yield exceeds the economic cost of 25bp. The strategic risks are asymmetric in severity rather than direction. On the base leg, if the market ever concludes the reaction function is politically rather than analytically determined, the dollar loses a credibility premium S&P explicitly cited in affirming AA+ on 26 June. On the quote leg, the January 2015 floor removal is the precedent that caps how far any SNB commitment can be trusted. Both are low-probability, high-severity, and both point the pair lower - which is why confidence is 60 rather than 70.

Tactically the case is a quantifiable arbitrage - a 34-43 percentage point gap between the June dots and the futures curve on the base leg, plus a written one-sided intervention option on the quote leg, resolving in a dated eight-day sequence. Strategically the same structures persist but two unquantifiable credibility tails appear, one on each leg, and both would push the pair lower rather than higher, which has to be paid for in confidence rather than in stance.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The four-week calendar is unusually dense for this pair and, unusually, the largest risks partly cancel rather than compound. The dominant scheduled item is the FOMC on 16 September with a Summary of Economic Projections attached - a genuine binary at 57-66% in futures against 48-55% in prediction markets - followed by the SNB assessment on 24 September and the Swiss constitutional neutrality referendum on 27 September, with US payrolls on 4 September and CPI on 11 September before all of them. The reason this factor is Neutral rather than Bullish is the haven-versus-haven structure of the geopolitical tail. Middle East escalation, which the July FOMC statement itself cited as a source of elevated uncertainty and which drove Brent from 100.31 to 88.24 in a month, is simultaneously dollar-positive on the haven and net-energy-export channels and franc-positive on the haven channel - so the largest undated risk in the window has an ambiguous sign for this specific pair, where a comparable analysis for a haven-versus-risk-proxy cross would be unambiguous. The genuinely bilateral, non-cancelling items are trade-policy items and they favour the pair: the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff regime is a live US-Switzerland dispute rather than a generic macro risk, and the USD 200bn Swiss investment commitment is a directly bilateral capital flow. The Swiss referendum is polling 62-36 against and is most likely a non-event, though passage would force a re-examination of Switzerland's alignment with the sanctions architecture under which CHF 8.5bn of assets are frozen. Probability-weighted, the tactical event expectation is close to zero and Neutral is the honest output.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the event set broadens and the ambiguity deepens. On the base leg the dominant scheduled event is the US midterm congressional election on 3 November, whose FX implication resists a directional call: a result constraining fiscal expansion is dollar-positive through the deficit channel and negative through growth, a result enabling it is the reverse, and the second-order question of how either outcome changes political pressure on a Fed that may have just hiked over presidential objection is unknowable in advance. The US tariff architecture is a second large binary - consolidation of the Section 301 structure is inflationary and pair-positive near-term, an unwind with refunds is disinflationary and pair-negative - and it cuts both ways. On the quote leg the strategic items are Bilaterals III ratification, signed on 2 March and now working through parliaments with a Swiss referendum possible, and the concentration of the Swiss banking system in a single institution after the 2023 Credit Suisse absorption, which is undated but systemic for the franc if it ever activates. Netting a two-sided election, a two-sided tariff resolution, a slow-burning EU ratification and a haven tail whose sign is ambiguous for a haven-versus-haven pair leaves no directional signal. Confidence is slightly lower than tactical because six months contains more opportunities for a tail to realise without making its direction any more predictable.

Tactically the calendar is dense and dated but the largest items either cancel across the two legs or are near-certain non-events; strategically the two largest items - a congressional election and a tariff legal resolution - are each genuinely two-sided, and averaging two ambiguous binaries produces Neutral rather than a direction.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The sovereign differential on this pair is close to the widest available in the G10 and it runs entirely against the pair, but over four weeks it is transmitting backwards, which is why the stance is Bearish at the lowest confidence in this analysis. The quote leg is AAA from every major agency, reconfirmed by Morningstar DBRS on 16 January 2026, with general government debt at 37.6% of GDP on the rating-agency measure (40.7% on the IMF's, nearer 30% on the Maastricht basis - the range is worth stating), a fiscal surplus of roughly 0.4% of GDP, a constitutional debt brake since 2003 and effectively no bond supply. The base leg is Aa1/AA+/AA+ with debt held by the public at 101% of GDP, a deficit above $2trn, projected fiscal-2026 interest costs of $1,039bn that would exceed the 1991 post-war high of 3.2% of GDP, and visibly deteriorating long-end auction reception - the 20-year stopping at 5.204% against 5.163% and the 30-year TIPS at 2.973% against 2.473%. On any measure of credit quality the quote leg wins overwhelmingly. But the tactical mechanism is inverted: on 1 September a global bond rout lifted yields, pushed gold to a ten-day low and lifted the dollar, so a deteriorating fiscal position is currently expressed as a dollar-supportive yield rise rather than a currency discount, and there is no Swiss fiscal event, rating review or Confederation auction of consequence inside the window to change that. The Bearish stance at 50 records a structural negative we do not expect to transmit over four weeks.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the weight rises to 0.07 and the character of the factor changes from absolute to relative, at which point the differential becomes a genuine drag on the pair. The mechanism that currently neutralises US fiscal deterioration - higher yields attracting capital - is the same mechanism that eventually breaks it, because interest costs compound automatically as low-coupon debt rolls into a 4.5-5.2% curve, and there is a direct and under-appreciated interaction with Factor 1: a September hike raises the front-end rollover cost, so the policy action that supports the pair tactically raises the fiscal burden that undermines it strategically. On the other leg nothing changes at all, and that is precisely the point - Switzerland's position does not improve, the alternatives deteriorate, and reserve managers and long-term allocators respond to relative rather than absolute quality. The bilateral expression problem is what caps confidence at 64: a 0.31% Swiss ten-year offers no way to express a quality preference through the bond market, so the preference has to be expressed in the currency, which is a slower and weaker channel than a bond bid. The genuine offset is that S&P's 26 June affirmation of AA+ explicitly cited credible, effective monetary policy execution, and a September hike reinforces exactly that credibility - so the base leg's rating backdrop is stable and provides no near-term catalyst in either direction.

The path of least resistance is a wide range with two regimes: pair-supported through the September-to-October policy window while the differential is at its widest, then contested into year-end as the surplus and the funding turn pull in opposite directions. Dated catalysts are the FOMC on 28 October and 9 December with SEP, the SNB on 10 December, the 3 November midterms and the 31 December funding turn. Conviction is 2 because both sides of the balance can be named precisely and neither can be sized, because a score 1.3 points above a threshold does not justify carrying outright directional risk for six months, and because the 200-week average at 0.85954 — 519 pips above spot and falling by less than a pip a week — is a standing structural obstacle that 84 weeks of price action have failed to overcome.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: USD/CHF drops materially in the strategic opportunity set, from a top-two long-dollar expression to roughly mid-table. The base dossier ranks the dollar fourth of eleven strategically, passed by SGD, NOK and SEK on external-balance strength; the quote dossier ranks the franc sixth of eleven, improved from ninth precisely because the criteria that matter over six months — a 9.77%-of-GDP current account, an AAA sovereign at 37.6% debt-to-GDP, a real effective rate at only the 40th percentile — are the ones it wins on. A pair whose base ranks fourth and whose quote ranks sixth is a mild positive, not a conviction long, and that is exactly what +0.1132 says. Among long-dollar crosses it now ranks behind USD/CAD, where the carry is smaller but the counterparty has no external offset, and behind the base dossier's preferred relative-value expressions. Among franc shorts it still beats CHF/JPY and CHF/SEK on carry but loses the strategic case against EUR/CHF once the ECB completes its cycle in late October, which is the quote dossier's own identified inflection.

strategic.path_expectation: The strategic path is a rounded double-top rather than a trend, and it is policy-dated. Phase one runs from now to late October and is the pair's strongest window: the differential is at its widest, the carry regime is intact with VIX at 14.4, and both legs' speculative positioning has room to be rebuilt. Expect the pair to test and possibly clear the 0.82072 52-week high in that phase, with the ActionForex 38.2% retracement at 0.8213 and the 0.8200 round number forming the practical ceiling on a first attempt. Phase two runs from November into January and should give part of it back as the market absorbs that the Committee's own 2027 median of 3.6% makes the September move terminal, with the 28 October FOMC — the first without a dot plot — as the specific inflection. Phase three is a renewed bid from late November into year-end driven not by rates but by funding, since reserves drifting toward $3trn with an empty reverse repo facility reproduce the December 2025 configuration, an episode that moved the dollar without moving the policy rate. Running beneath all three phases is a persistent structural franc bid from a 12.6-point current-account differential and the 146 pips of carry accruing in the pair's favour, which is why the window ends only modestly above spot but well above the forward. The pullback levels to watch on the way are the top of the six-touch band at 0.80001 and then the 200-day at 0.79348; volatility should rise through the horizon simply because 7.187% six-month implied is too low for a pair with this distribution.

consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Our view differs in sign, not merely magnitude. The reason we differ is a premise, not a forecast: every bearish write-up we can source attributes the expected fall to Fed easing, and that premise has been falsified four separate ways — the June dot plot raised the 2026 median to 3.8% from 3.4%, the July meeting produced a 9-3 hold with all three dissenters wanting a hike, Warsh's 28 August keynote said underlying inflation trends have not meaningfully improved while quoting headline PCE at 3.7% and 4.1% annualised over six months, and the 2-year Treasury at 4.34% sits 71.5bp above the policy midpoint. The bilateral factor we weight differently is Factor 1, boosted to 0.27, because one leg is pinned at zero by a three-year conditional forecast while the other has a live hiking bias: consensus treats the differential as fated to compress and we treat it as fated to persist. The bilateral factor we weight no less heavily than consensus does is Factor 5 — a 12.6-point current-account differential is a genuine constraint, and it is precisely why our strategic conviction is 2 rather than 4. Consensus barely differs from the forward at one month, which means the consensus view is the carry view at short horizons and only becomes a genuine directional call further out.

consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If consensus is right and the Fed holds or eases, the pair falls while the base leg's 18,682-contract net long is stranded and the quote leg's remaining short is squeezed — the two legs' positioning amplify rather than cushion each other in that direction. The persistent negative risk reversal at every tenor says the market is already paying for exactly that outcome, and the strategic version is worse: a hike delivered and then reversed into a labour market already shedding payrolls would combine a base-leg policy mistake with a quote-leg structural bid.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: Aligned on direction but sharply divergent on strength — a 71% decay between horizons, larger than either dossier shows on its own. The mechanism is the reweighting rather than a change of view: External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16 and turns a −0.0330 contribution into −0.1120, Inflation and Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10 and turns Neutral as both legs' borrowed data strength unwinds, and Factor 1's confidence falls from 74 to 60 because the Committee's own 2027 median of 3.6% makes a September hike terminal rather than the start of a cycle. So the same 362.5bp differential that is a widening impulse over four weeks becomes a static cost over six months, at which point Switzerland's balance sheet is nearly large enough to offset it.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Late October to early November 2026, specifically the FOMC on 28 October — the first meeting after September without a Summary of Economic Projections attached and therefore the first at which the market must judge on the Committee's silence whether the hike was terminal. A secondary, quote-side marker is Q4 Swiss data, where the pharmaceutical front-running that inflated Q2 GDP and the record July trade surplus should begin to reverse.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Treat the tactical view as a position with an expiry rather than the opening leg of a strategic one. The information event that resolves the tactical trade — the 16 September dot plot — is the same release that sets the strategic path. Because the pair's volatility surface carries no event premium in either direction, there is no timing argument for waiting for the cluster to resolve. Practically: size the tactical leg on ATR with a stop below 0.7955, take the base-case profit into the 0.8207-0.8213 confluence rather than holding through it, and hold any residual strategic exposure at roughly a quarter of tactical size with the six-touch 0.79288-0.80001 band as the structural line.

catalysts.event: US August non-farm payrolls, unemployment rate and average hourly earnings (consensus +58,000 after −23,000)
catalysts.rationale: The largest data risk before the FOMC and the single event most capable of removing the pair's principal support. A second consecutive contraction would make a hike twelve days later very difficult to defend, collapsing Factors 1, 2 and 6 together — the three that supply the bulk of the tactical score. The quote leg has no equivalent release, so the transmission is entirely one-sided: the pair reprices on the base leg's reaction function while the SNB remains pinned at zero regardless of the outcome.

catalysts.event: SNB foreign currency reserves for August and SECO Swiss unemployment
catalysts.rationale: Reserves rose from CHF 759bn to CHF 768bn between June and July, but with the franc weakening and gold up 8.6% on the month that build is more consistent with valuation and income than with active intervention. A further large rise while the franc is soft would suggest the SNB is building capacity rather than defending a level, which is pair-positive at the margin; Swiss unemployment drifting above 3.1% would soften the growth story that is currently the quote leg's only support.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with staff projections (third-currency event)
catalysts.rationale: A 25bp increase to a 2.50% deposit rate is close to fully priced and would take the euro-franc policy spread from 225bp to 250bp. That matters for USD/CHF second-hand rather than directly: it pulls franc selling into EUR/CHF, which is the cleaner and better-carried expression of the same short-franc view, and a hawkish outcome would make the euro cross the preferred vehicle at this pair's expense. Conversely, an explicit signal that the euro-area cycle is complete would remove the quote leg's largest external pressure and is the most likely September source of franc strength.

catalysts.event: US August CPI (July base 3.4% headline, 2.5% core) and monthly federal budget balance
catalysts.rationale: The last inflation print before the FOMC, and the configuration is unusual in a way that matters for the pair: core CPI at 2.5% sits 80bp below core PCE at 3.3%, an inversion of the normal relationship, so a soft core CPI print is less dovish than it appears because the Fed targets PCE and Warsh quoted headline PCE at 3.7%. Against a quote leg running 0.4% headline inflation, any print that keeps the roughly 300bp differential intact keeps the base leg's reaction function engaged and the pair supported.

catalysts.event: Federal Reserve FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The dominant event for this pair. Futures price roughly 57-66% odds of a 25bp increase to 3.75-4.00% while the June dot median of 3.8% implies it outright and prediction markets carry 48-55%; delivery takes the bilateral differential from 362.5bp to 387.5bp against a quote leg that cannot respond. The attached dot plot simultaneously sets the strategic path, since a 2027 median held at 3.6% makes the move terminal — so this single release resolves the tactical trade and calibrates the strategic one. The pair's volatility surface carries no premium for it.

catalysts.event: Swiss trade balance for August (July: CHF 8.1bn nominal, the largest surplus since 1950)
catalysts.rationale: The dated test of whether Switzerland's record surplus is structural or Section 232 front-running. A second consecutive print above CHF 7bn would force the balance-of-payments story into a narrative currently dominated by carry and would strengthen the pair's largest strategic negative; a sharp fall would confirm that July's 25.7% jump in pharmaceutical exports was demand pulled forward ahead of the 31 July tariff date, which is pair-positive on a six-month view.

catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank quarterly monetary policy assessment with refreshed conditional inflation forecast
catalysts.rationale: A hold at 0.00% is effectively certain, so the entire tradeable content is the language. The June statement's increased willingness to intervene against rapid and excessive franc appreciation was written when the franc was under upward pressure; after a 3.58% six-month depreciation against the dollar that pressure has evidently abated, and dropping or softening the sentence would be read as tolerance of a stronger franc and would remove the one-sided option that supplies most of Factor 6. The sequencing is important: this lands eight days after the FOMC, so the SNB is responding to whatever level the Fed produces.

catalysts.event: Swiss federal referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality
catalysts.rationale: Polling at roughly 62% against and 36% in favour (August Tamedia/20 Minuten, flagged as best available), so rejection is the strong base case and the modal outcome is a non-event. Passage would bar Switzerland from joining sanctions absent a UN mandate and force a re-examination of the framework under which CHF 8.5bn of assets are frozen, cutting both ways for the franc's haven premium — arguably enhancing the neutrality claim while raising market-access friction. A roughly 20% tail is being carried for free, since no event premium appears in the pair's volatility surface.

catalysts.event: September US dollar quarter-end funding date
catalysts.rationale: The first quarter-end since reserve balances resumed falling, at $2,916bn and heading toward the roughly $3trn minimum comfortable level with the reverse repo facility drained to $702mn. For this pair specifically, tighter dollar funding forces franc-funded carry positions to be bought back in dollars, which is the one shock that resolves a haven-versus-haven pair decisively upward rather than ambiguously. The December 2025 precedent saw standing repo usage reach a record $74.6bn.

catalysts.event: Federal Reserve FOMC decision, no Summary of Economic Projections attached
catalysts.rationale: The identified inflection between the two horizons on this pair. It is the first meeting after September without a dot plot, so the market must judge on the Committee's silence whether the September move was terminal — the question on which the entire 71% decay in score between the tactical and strategic readings turns. A statement that keeps a further move live would push the strategic score well clear of the Neutral boundary; confirmation of a terminal hike leaves it where it is, at +0.1132.

The dominant scheduled event of the strategic window and genuinely two-sided for this pair. A result constraining fiscal expansion is pair-positive through the deficit channel and negative through growth; a result enabling it is the reverse. The second-order question — how either outcome changes political pressure on a Fed that may have just hiked over presidential objection, and therefore on the credibility premium the quote leg does not need — is unknowable in advance. No volatility premium exists at any tenor covering the date.

catalysts.event: Federal Reserve FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The final base-leg event of the strategic window and the release at which the 2027 median dot — currently 3.6%, implying a cut back from a September hike — is either confirmed or removed. Confirmation validates the low-conviction strategic reading; removal converts the September move from terminal into a cycle and would take the pair's largest positive factor from a plateau back to a widening impulse, which is the specific trigger to upgrade the strategic stance.

catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank quarterly monetary policy assessment with new conditional inflation forecast
catalysts.rationale: Landing one day after the FOMC, this is the second occasion in the window on which the two banks decide inside 24 hours, and the sequencing again favours the base leg setting the tone. The rate is all but certain to remain at 0.00%; the variables are the intervention language and any revision to the 2027-2028 forecast path. A downward revision toward zero inflation would reopen the negative-rate tail that Schlegel has dismissed and would be sharply pair-positive.

The direct analogue of the December 2025 episode, when SOFR-to-IORB spreads reached their widest since 2020 and standing repo usage spiked to a record $74.6bn before collapsing to zero in January. Both dossiers independently identify it as the most reliable seasonal source of basis widening, and it is unusually pair-relevant: a widening basis forces the reduction of positions funded in the zero-rate leg, which is mechanically pair-positive on both sides at once. Full-allotment standing repo operations should cap it at pressure rather than crisis.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting with Outlook Report (third-currency event)
catalysts.rationale: The most likely venue for the next BoJ hike, and it matters for this pair through the funding-rotation channel rather than through any direct linkage. Swiss rates are currently 0% and Japanese rates 1%; a move to 1.25% widens that gap and reinforces the franc's role as the cheaper funding leg — which is pair-positive in the short run but pair-negative in the medium run, because it deepens the concentrated short that Factor 4 identifies as squeeze fuel. Just outside the six-month window but close enough to shape year-end positioning.

Moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes computed over the whole stored history, not over the 130 visible bars: 50-day 0.80918, 100-day 0.79934, 200-day 0.79348, 200-week 0.85954 with a slope of −0.000925 per week and 84 weeks since the last close above. The 200-week average is treated as a first-class structural level; its near-flat slope is the reason it is characterised as a standing obstacle rather than a converging one.

Support and resistance are the payload's computed zones only. No web-sourced level has been used. Zone distances are measured to zone midpoints. Web research was used only for named chart patterns requiring visual identification (the Dukascopy ascending channel, the horizontal medium-term channel reading, and the 38.2% retracement at 0.8213), flagged as pattern references rather than levels.

Implied volatility, risk reversals and the funding premium are taken verbatim from the gated derived store, not from web search: implied vol observed 2026-08-31 by cme_atm method at 38.6/94.7/185.7 days, and funding premium −415.8bp annualised observed 2026-08-31 by cme_calendar_spread over 13.6 to 104.7 days. The 3-month ATM figure of 7.031% is measured at 94.7 days rather than 90 because CME lists quarterly. Forward points and outrights are derived by applying the −415.8bp premium linearly across tenors and will differ from a dealer quote by the term structure of the basis. The roughly 53.3bp residual over the 362.5bp policy differential cannot be decomposed into basis versus money-market spread without an OIS curve.

Both legs' ten-year yields are MONTHLY observations dated 2026-06-01 (USD 4.47% via IRLTLT01USM156N, CHF 0.31% via IRLTLT01CHM156N), so the +416bp long-end differential is a like-for-like vintage comparison and not a live spread. The base dossier's own cross-checks found cached peer yields understating live levels by 35-47bp. Policy rates are as of 2026-09-01 (CBPOL_US 3.625% midpoint of 3.50-3.75%, CBPOL_CH 0.00%), so the 362.5bp differential is a midpoint reading; a range-based reading would give 350-375bp.

Bilateral trade is the injected IMF DOTS block for 2024 and has not been re-estimated from the web. It is goods only — no services, no FDI, no portfolio flows — which materially understates the true bilateral relationship for a pair where one leg's surplus is substantially services and primary income. The two directions differ ($63.7bn of US imports from Switzerland against $73.5bn of Swiss exports to the US) because of valuation and re-export treatment, and the US net figure of −$38.6bn is the one used.

Weight adjustments: +0.03 to Factor 1 on both horizons for the high-carry, one-leg-pinned-at-zero structure; −0.03 tactical and −0.02 strategic to Factor 3 for the haven-versus-haven muting; −0.01 strategic to Factor 9. All are within the ±0.05 limit and both horizons sum to exactly 1.00. Net stance on both horizons is derived mechanically from net_weighted_score using the framework's thresholds; the strategic score of +0.1132 clears the +0.10 threshold by 1.3 points and is stated as Bullish accordingly, with the fragility argued in the score interpretation rather than resolved by relabelling.

Factor stances, confidences, evidence types and analyses are carried verbatim from pass 1 and have not been re-scored, re-weighted or reworded. Pass 1 was scored without the price payload, deliberately, so that a stance could not be reverse-engineered from a chart. Where the now-visible payload adds material pass 1 could not use — principally the trend structure, the zones and the 200-week slope in Factor 9 — that material appears as a labelled note rather than as a change to the score.

Pair-specific data limitations: 25-delta risk reversals ARE available from the gated store (an improvement on both dossiers). Option barrier levels and dealer-known round-number interest could not be sourced and are recorded as a gap. The direct 3-month CHF/USD cross-currency basis is unquoted; only the derived residual is available. Positioning carries an observation-date caveat: the −19.9k aggregate is the 28 August release covering a 25 August observation while the internal split is from the 11 August tranche, so the −38,322 asset-manager figure is an upper bound. There is an unresolved conflict between the covering narrative and fresher research reporting hedge-fund franc shorts at a two-month high; the two are different measures on different vintages and the conflict is flagged rather than reconciled. Bank consensus targets reach this report via an aggregator page whose individual house attributions the quote dossier's own verification found partly unsupported. Referendum polling of 62-36 comes from an August poll that could not be tied to a free primary link. Swiss general government debt is 37.6% on the rating-agency measure, 40.7% on the IMF's and nearer 30% on the Maastricht basis.

Scenario probabilities, invalidator probabilities and target levels are analyst judgements calibrated to the factor analysis and the payload's zone structure, not derived from options-implied distributions. Position-sizing figures are illustrative arithmetic on stated stop distances and ATR(14) = 55 pips, not recommendations.
